_comment: Toolchain pin for the layout/ verification flow (klt drc / klt extract /
klt lvs), checked (not merely recorded) before either runner does
anything -- the layout/ analogue of sim/toolchain.json's ngspice/PDK pin.
Why this is a CAPABILITY list, not a version number: `klt --version`
reports klayout-tools' own static pyproject.toml version, which moves
only when upstream cuts one -- it did not change across the ~150
commits between issue #15's pin and #51's ('0.1.0' at both), and this
pin's own bump moved it only from '0.1.0' to '0.2.0' while adding four
capabilities this repo depends on. A version string comparison would
therefore silently pass against a `klt` that is missing something this
repo needs. `klt_required_commands` is the coarse drift-detectable pin:
both runners look every entry up in `klt --help`'s subcommand list
before doing anything else and fail loudly, with the install command in
the error text, if one is missing -- exercised directly by running the
#51 bring-up against the release issue #15 pinned (no `extract`/`lvs`)
before upgrading. One shared implementation, in
`layout/toolchain_pin.py`, imported by both `layout/drc/run_drc.py` and
`layout/lvs/run_lvs.py` -- a per-runner copy would let the two drift
apart, and this claim is only worth making if it is true of both.
A verb list is NOT sufficient on its own any more, and that gap is
closed where it can be seen rather than argued: this repo now depends
on the gf180mcu extraction DECK recognising a device class
(`cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield`), which every `klt` since `lvs` landed has
the verbs for. `layout/lvs/cells/cells.json`'s `extract.expect.
device_classes` pins the deck's own declared class list and
`run_lvs.py` asserts it, so an install from before that recognition
landed fails with a named mismatch instead of silently extracting the
CDAC unit capacitor as ordinary interconnect (issue #70).
Why `klt_install` names an exact commit and not a floating `git+URL`:
verified directly while implementing #51 that `main` is not safe to
float against here -- an upstream deck gaining coverage is a change
this repo's committed negative controls and manifests have to absorb
deliberately, in one reviewed change, not silently on the next
reinstall.
THIS PIN (issue #70) is that deliberate absorption, and it crosses two
upstream changes the previous pin (`e08f24f`) deliberately sat before:
* `1d5fc60` (PR #192) added gf180mcu DRC coverage for the MiM
capacitor stack and Metal2-5/MetalTop. It is what makes
`layout/drc/cells/uncovered_layer_probe.gds` -- issue #15's negative
control, drawn to prove the deck was NOT looking at those layers --
report real violations. `cells.json`'s expectations for that cell
are re-baselined in the same change, from `clean` to the four rules
it now catches. That is `layout/README.md`'s own 'useful failure:
it tells us the gap closed', taken.
* `0aa8bc2`/`fd22b7d` (PRs #238/#235) populated the extraction deck's
full Metal1-Metal5 / Via1-Via4 stack and added MiM capacitor device
recognition. Together they are what let a drawn unit capacitor be a
CHECKED device instead of three inert polygons.
and picks up `c6fa8b8`/`de4b8dc` (`klt extract --parasitics`) on the
way, which is what issue #17 needs and could not have without this bump.
THE ISSUE #116 PIN (`875eac3`) is the third deliberate absorption, and
it crosses exactly one upstream change the previous pin (`af5791b`) sat
before -- `875eac3` IS upstream `main`'s HEAD as of 2026-08-06, 29
commits ahead of `af5791b` and 0 behind:
* `2AMLogic/klayout-tools#593` ("feat(extract): star-topology
parasitic resistance in --parasitics"), which closed
`klayout-tools#592` COMPLETED. Before it, `klt extract
--parasitics` wrote each net's whole resistance as ONE dead-end
stub (`R<net> <net> <net>__par`, with `<net>__par` reached only by
the net's own `C`), so NO device terminal ever sat behind it and
the resistance carried no signal current -- structurally proven in
`adc-top/parasitics/records/20260806-parasitic-topology.md` and
visible as `sim/device-switch-ron/`'s post-layout R_on delta of
exactly zero across all 1125 result cells. After it, every device
terminal on a net gets its own leg node (`<net>__t<k>`) with a
distance-weighted series resistor back to the hub, so two terminals
on one net are separated by real, layout-dependent resistance.
`klayout-tools#594` was a competing even-split implementation of
the same request: CLOSED without merging (re-verified live
2026-08-06), so `#593` is the change that landed and nothing here
depends on `#594`.
Full distributed per-segment RC (`#592`'s Option 2) remains
explicitly OUT of scope upstream -- this pin buys in-path
resistance, not a distributed RC line model, and
`adc-top/parasitics/records/20260806-parasitic-topology-inpath.md`
says so in the same breath as reporting the numbers it does buy.
Two committed baselines move BECAUSE of this bump and are re-baselined
in the same change, deliberately, not silently:
* `layout/drc/cells/uncovered_layer_probe.gds` -- issue #15's
negative control -- now additionally reports `via4.width.1` (x2)
and `metal4.enclosing.via4.1`, 8 violations -> 11. Same "useful
failure: the gap closed" as the #70 MiM/Metal bump.
* every extraction's `warnings` list grows (the deck now names each
unbiased PMOS body net and each unmodelled poly shape individually
instead of summarising), and `--parasitics` r_count grows by
roughly one R per device terminal. Device/net/pin counts are
unchanged everywhere except `adc_block`, whose net_count moves
198 -> 196 for an unrelated reason (issue #116's own comparator
input-connectivity fix).
THE ISSUE #173 BUMP WAS ATTEMPTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN, and this
paragraph is the record of that decision so a later reader does not
re-derive it. `klt pex` (`klayout-tools` epic #709, closed 2026-08-14)
ships in upstream `main` at `755d3ef` and is NOT reachable under this
pin, so #173 asked to bump onto it. The bump was tried live, against
this repo's own committed baselines, and is not the mechanical
absorption it looks like from the outside:
* `klt lvs` itself is unaffected -- every case in
`layout/lvs/cells/cells.json` still reports `mismatches=0` against
a FRESH extraction under `755d3ef`.
* but `klt extract`'s OUTPUT SHAPE moves twice inside the range.
`af58e41` (`klayout-tools#697`) puts MOS junction AS/AD/PS/PD on
every `--pdk-bound` X card (`as_um2`/`ad_um2`/`ps_um2`/`pd_um2`,
absent under this pin), and `10c6eca` (`klayout-tools#603`)
re-aggregates the per-instance `warnings[]` entries the #116
paragraph above describes this pin as having introduced. So every
committed `.spice` netlist snapshot (`adc_top`, `adc_block`,
`comparator`, `comparator_nores`) and both manifests' `expect`
blocks (`layout/drc/cells/*.json`, `layout/lvs/cells/cells.json`)
go stale simultaneously -- and those snapshots are not only LVS
fixtures, they are parsed for their exact pin lists by the #89-era
extracted-core testbench generators (`gen_extracted_core_tb.py` et
al.). That re-baseline has the blast radius of the #70/#116 bumps
above, so it gets its own reviewed change rather than riding on
`pex` is likewise deliberately ABSENT from `klt_required_commands`:
an entry there makes EVERY layout/ runner (drc, lvs, extraction) refuse
to start, and the still-pinned `875eac3` install cannot satisfy it.
#173's own `klt pex` evidence therefore runs against a separate,
investigative pin (`layout/adc-top/parasitics/run_pex_comparator.py`'s
`PEX_KLT_COMMIT`) and is recorded in `sim/comparator-pex/`. What it
found is that `klt pex` is blocked for every block this repo extracts,
for a reason no pin bump changes -- its DUT-swap requires the schematic
and extracted top-level `.subckt` interfaces to be pin-identical, which
`klt extract`'s promoted body/tap/internal nets never are here
(`klayout-tools#1030`). This pin is not what stands between T1 item 7
and a pass.
THE ISSUE #178 PIN (`85b8125`) is the fourth deliberate absorption --
the bump #173 above found was not mechanical, done properly with its
own re-baseline. `klt pdk find` still resolves `gf180mcuA` in this
environment; nothing about PDK resolution changed. Re-verified LIVE at
pickup time (2026-08-16) rather than pinning `173`'s own `755d3ef`
verbatim: `85b8125` IS upstream `main`'s HEAD as of 2026-08-16, 17
commits ahead of `755d3ef` and 0 behind -- including one more DRC-deck
fix in-range (`be190e3`, "scope gf180mcu mim.space.1 to the MiM
virtual bottom plate") that a `755d3ef` pin would have sat in front
of. Checked directly: it does not move a single rule_counts value this
repo's DRC proof cells report (`layout/drc/cells/cells.json` needed NO
re-baseline at all -- every cell, including `uncovered_layer_probe`'s
`mim.space.1` count, is byte-identical before and after).
CORRECTION to the #173 paragraph above: its claim that "every
committed `.spice` netlist snapshot ... go[es] stale simultaneously"
does not hold. Verified directly by re-extracting all ten committed
LVS snapshots (`adc_top`, `adc_block`, `comparator`, `comparator_nores`,
and the five `layout/adc-top/cells/*.spice` leaf cells, plus
`layout/lvs/cells/lvs_unit.spice`) under `85b8125` with no `--pdk`
flag -- exactly how `run_lvs.py` extracts them -- and diffing byte for
byte: EVERY one is identical to what was already committed. `af58e41`
(`klayout-tools#697`) only puts `AS=`/`AD=`/`PS=`/`PD=` junction-area/
perimeter params on `--pdk`-BOUND X cards; `run_lvs.py` never passes
`--pdk`, so its netlist TEXT never gained them. What DOES change is the
JSON extraction SUMMARY's `devices[].params` (present regardless of
`--pdk`, confirmed on `lvs_unit`'s single device) and `warnings[]`
shape (`10c6eca`, `klayout-tools#603`) -- fields `cells.json`'s
`expect` blocks pin, not the `.spice` files themselves. No `.spice`
snapshot moved; none is re-committed by this pin.
CAVEAT to the paragraph above, added during PR #195 Judge review
(2026-08-16): the byte-for-byte match was verified on Linux x86_64 /
Python 3.12 -- this repo's own canonical environment (both CI's
`ubuntu-latest` runners and every committed `layout/*/reports/*/
toolchain.json` snapshot agree; see e.g. this pin's own
`adc-top/parasitics/reports/20260816-174824-539f5d9/toolchain.json`).
Re-running the identical `klt extract` on a DIFFERENT host during
review did NOT reproduce byte-identical: `adc_top`'s extraction
swapped two anonymous net labels (`$171`/`$172`, across six device
terminals), while `klt lvs` itself still reported `mismatches=0` for
that same extraction -- connectivity was unaffected, only the
arbitrary label assigned to an unlabeled promoted net differed. This
is NOT a regression from this pin: the identical drift class was
already confirmed pre-existing on an unmodified `origin/main` GDS
during PR #88's review (2026-08-05, Linux vs. macOS Darwin arm64 /
Python 3.14.6) -- it is `klt extract`'s anonymous/synthetic net
numbering (labels assigned to a promoted net with no source layout
label, e.g. a MOS body/tap net) not being guaranteed stable across
host platform / Python version at a fixed topology. Filed upstream
as `klayout-tools#1063`.
`layout/lvs/run_lvs.py --check`'s byte-for-byte assertion is
deliberately left strict rather than loosened to tolerate this --
weakening it would also hide a REAL extraction regression -- but a
reported `[FAIL]` that is ONLY an anonymous-net-label swap, with
`klt lvs mismatches=0` unaffected, is this known environment-
dependent drift, not evidence the committed netlist is wrong. Also
worth noting: no CI workflow in this repo actually installs `klt` and
runs `run_lvs.py --check` -- `ci.yml` only python-syntax-checks
`layout/` (no PDK/`klt` install), and `nightly-pdk.yml` covers
`sim/`'s ngspice/PDK pin only -- so this drift is invisible to CI
either way and only surfaces when a human or agent reviewer re-runs
the check on a different machine.
`layout/lvs/cells/cells.json` DOES need re-baselining, on exactly those
two JSON-summary fields, done with a new `run_lvs.py --regen-manifest`
(mirroring `run_extract_parasitics.py`'s own flag; `run_drc.py` needed
no equivalent -- see above, its manifest did not move):
* `lvs_unit`'s one device gains `as_um2`/`ad_um2`/`ps_um2`/`pd_um2` in
its JSON `params` (`1.68`/`1.584`/`5.2`/`5.04` -- the physical
junction geometry `af58e41` now reports for a 1.2u/0.28u nfet;
this repo draws no differently, the field is simply new).
* every block's `warnings[]` re-aggregates further: the per-device
`{"contains": "body ties to anonymous net", "count": n}` counted
form the #116 paragraph above describes collapses into ONE
fully-aggregated string per class (`10c6eca`) -- `adc_top` goes
from 150 warning entries to 4, `adc_block` from 162 to 5. Two NEW
diagnostic classes appear, both investigated, both confirmed to be
restating already-known, already-handled facts rather than new
findings:
- `dead_metal` (`klayout-tools#681`) reports 210 Metal1/Metal4
clusters joining no net, identically on `adc_top` and
`adc_block`. Cross-checked against `gen_adc_top.py`'s own CDAC
dummy-ring geometry (`_draw_side()`'s docstring: "the dummy
ring stays `device=False` -- inert, floating geometry for edge
matching only", ARRAY_COLS=32 x ARRAY_ROWS=16 with a one-tile
ring on both array sides is (34x18-32x16)*2=200, within 10 of
the reported 210) -- this is the ALREADY-INTENDED unconnected
dummy ring, newly named rather than newly present. Not caught
by (and does not contradict) `klt lvs`'s independent
`mismatches=0`: dead metal is by definition metal no device
terminal reaches, so a REQUIRED connection going missing would
surface as an LVS mismatch, not merely as more dead metal.
- `single_terminal_nets` (`klayout-tools#601`) reports 1-2 nets
per block. Checked directly against each block's own
`unbiased_pmos_body_nets[]`: same device, same net, in every
case (e.g. `comparator`'s device `$18`'s body net `$22` is
named by both diagnostics) -- a second, more generic lens on
the SAME already-known, already-remediated PMOS-body-to-
anonymous-net gap (`remediate_extracted.py`, `klayout-
tools#555`), not a distinct finding.
`layout/adc-top/parasitics/cells.json` (`run_extract_parasitics.py`)
needed NO re-baseline of its existing `r_count`/`c_count`/device-tally
fields -- all unchanged -- but a live re-run surfaced a real gap those
counts cannot see: `b40955d` (`klayout-tools#764`, "model
vertical-overlap (crossover) coupling capacitance for --parasitics",
issue #760) changes which nets a coupled net pair's overlap
capacitance is charged to (net-to-net instead of double-counted as
ground fringe on each side) WITHOUT moving `c_count` at all -- the
element count is unchanged, only the VALUES are. Measured directly:
`adc_top` total extracted capacitance moves 5215.82fF -> 5154.95fF
and `adc_block` 5622.31fF -> 5561.44fF (both ~1.1-1.2% down);
`adc_tgate`, small enough that none of its four nets shares a coupled
overlap, is unaffected. Total resistance is unaffected everywhere
(no upstream change in range touches R). This is a real accuracy
improvement, not a connectivity or geometry change -- but it is
exactly the "new shape masks a real behavior change" gap a count-only
assertion cannot catch, so `check_block()`/`regen_manifest()` now also
assert/regenerate `parasitics.total_resistance_ohm`/
`total_capacitance_ff`, closing the gap for the next bump rather than
leaving it to be re-discovered by hand again.
A new parasitics record (`20260816-174824-539f5d9`) was minted under
this pin, becoming `remediate_extracted.py`'s `_latest_report()` --
every #89-era extracted-core generator that reads it
(`gen_extracted_core_tb.py`, `gen_extracted_dr0014_sampling_tb.py`,
`gen_extracted_enob_fft_tb.py`, `gen_extracted_inl_dnl_tb.py`,
`gen_extracted_power_tb.py`, `gen_extracted_switch_ron_tb.py`) was
re-run and its committed `sim/.../tb_*_extracted.spice` output
re-generated and re-committed; every generator's own `--check` (byte-
identity against the committed file) is clean again. The diff in each
is exactly the `AS=`/`AD=`/`PS=`/`PD=` device-card additions plus the
new `7c5cef8` parasitic-model header comment (`klayout-tools#728`) --
nothing else. `gen_extracted_switch_ron_tb.py`'s own `_EXTRACT_DEV`
regex broke on this (it end-anchored `W=(\S+)\s*$`, assuming `W=` was
always the LAST token on a device line -- no longer true once `AS=`/
`AD=`/`PS=`/`PD=` follow it); fixed by dropping the anchor, since this
module only ever reads the four terminal nets, the model name, and
`L=`/`W=`. `gen_extracted_timing_budget_tb.py` was already up to date
(it does not embed device X-cards directly, only R/C timing constants
derived from them).
OUT OF SCOPE for this pin bump, called out rather than silently
assumed: the AS/AD/PS/PD junction params and the ~1.1-1.2% capacitance
shift above are REAL SPICE-model inputs, not cosmetic text -- a full
PVT-corner re-run of the six regenerated `sim/` experiments (INL/DNL,
ENOB/FFT, power, DR-0014 gain error, switch R_on, and whatever
`gen_extracted_timing_budget_tb.py` feeds) to see whether any spec-line
claim in `sim/extracted-delta-summary.md` moves is NOT done here -- it
is a materially larger undertaking (six PVT sweeps, new append-only
sim/ records each) than a manifest re-baseline, and `verify_
extracted_core_conversion.py`'s own single-corner transient check (run
directly against the regenerated extracted core: it still converts) is
the bound this issue substantiates instead. A fast-follow issue should
re-run the affected experiments' PVT batteries if a numeric
re-verification of their spec-line claims under this pin is wanted.
`pex` remains deliberately ABSENT from `klt_required_commands`, for the
same reason the #173 paragraph above gives: `klayout-tools#1030`'s
DUT-swap pin-identity requirement is untouched by this bump, so `klt
pex` is still blocked for every block this repo extracts. Not
re-verified against `85b8125` here -- #173's own investigative pin
already answered the question this pin bump does not change the
answer to.
klt_install            exact commit to install `klt` from -- a `pip`/
`uv tool install` VCS URL pinned with `@<sha>`
(no PyPI release yet, ../README.md), not a
floating branch reference. See above for why
floating is unsafe for this repo specifically.
klt_required_commands  every `klt <command>` this repo's layout/
runners invoke. A missing one is a tooling
error (exit 1) from *either* runner, not a
silently-skipped check. Adding an entry here is
all it takes to make both runners require it.
klt_last_verified_commit  the exact commit `klt_install` resolves to,
restated here so it is visible without
parsing the install URL. Update both together
and re-run both runners' --check when bumping.
klayout_package_min    floor for the pip `klayout` package version
(`klayout_tools`' own `pyproject.toml` pins
`klayout>=0.29`); recorded here so a drift in
*this* repo's pin is visible next to `klt`'s.
A drift in `klt_required_commands` is fatal by default; there is no
--allow-toolchain-drift override here (unlike sim/toolchain.json) --
layout/ evidence is cheap enough to regenerate that skipping the check
has no use case yet.
